subject: inverting mesh interior from s2 mesh object with boundary

messages.author: ef409dbd3be2e2c7
messages.subject: inverting mesh interior from s2 mesh object with boundary
parts:
Hi, inla discussion group,

First of all, thank you for developing and continuing this amazing software.

I am having trouble generating mesh on s2(unit sphere) with boundary.
I have a segment that I don't want my mesh to be inside, but I have no idea how to control it.
For example, what I want to do is that create a globe mesh without the States, but the opposite is keep happening.
How can I fix this?

For your reference, I have attached a picture for the current status and a segment file.
Thank you in advance for your comments.

Yours Sincerely,
Minho.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inverting mesh interior from s2 mesh object with boundary
parts:
Hi,
Inside/outside is determined by the direction your boundary is traversed. To exclude a region, the boundary definition needs to circle the region in clockwise order. “Inside” is defined as the region that is encircled in a counterclockwise order. So if you get the opposite effect to what you want, then reverse order of your boundary points, and try again!

Finn
